I have a yellow monopoly with uneven house counts: Ventnor Avenue and Marvin Gardens each have one house, while Atlantic Avenue has none. I also own Park Place and two unmortgaged orange properties.

I can only build on Atlantic Avenue because of the even-building rule. p1 has four railroads and a mortgaged Boardwalk with $168 cash. p2 has incomplete pink and red monopolies plus utilities and two GOOJF cards with $240 cash. p3 is the main threat with a full light-blue hotel monopoly, an incomplete brown set, and an incomplete green set, plus $3214 cash.

I will not build on Atlantic Avenue or unmortgage orange properties. I will not sell New York, Pennsylvania, Mediterranean, yellow, or orange holdings. I need to survive the next lap and only layer yellow if roughly two hundred dollars remain after building. This is turn 117.

I am deciding whether to trade. The goal is three yellow houses to pressure p3, but cash of 229 is too thin to survive light-blue hotels and four railroads.

I cannot safely build. Trading with p3 would be risky because they could complete the brown set and hotel it immediately with their $3214 cash. I must never give them Mediterranean Avenue. Trading Park Place to p1 would complete their dark blue monopoly, but that is too dangerous.

I will end the turn without trading. I cannot find a deal that gives me enough cash to build yellow safely.

Even a large cash payment from selling Mediterranean Avenue would not cover the $1050 needed to reach three yellow houses. The mortgage buffer would also be lost.

Mortgaging all mortgageable properties would yield only $534, still short of the $1050 needed for three yellow houses. Even reaching two houses on each yellow property would require $600, leaving me broke with mortgaged holdings. I am now checking the exact rent values for a two-house yellow set.

A single house on Atlantic Avenue would raise rent from $52 to $130, but the $150 cost is too steep for my thin cash. I will end the turn.
